mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months signals a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction, reducing equity risk appetite and compressing discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rate hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 1% month-over-month signals weakening labor market strength, lowering consumer confidence and equity valuations, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in labor weakening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
